# The commit search tolerates the one path the procedure forces, and a RED's tree is unfindable by construction

RED is record 51 and GREEN is record 53; green 52 is also true but was recorded before a comment reword moved the
tree by one line, and 53 is the green whose tree is the tree that will be committed, which is exactly the property
this fix makes load-bearing. The RED's semantic mirror failed as it had to, on a fixture committed exactly as the
procedure requires, checks then the Outcome then the commit: "'harness/slice_one.py' not found in 'The tree moved
under check 3 ... compared over the whole tree because no commit on this branch carries the tree it ran against'".
A scope that should have been granted and then refused by name fell back to the whole tree instead.

**The fingerprint is untouched and `FINGERPRINT_EXCLUDED` is untouched.** Only the search for the commit carrying
a check's tree became tolerant, of exactly one path: the ticket file, resolved the same way the triage resolves it.
The argument for that path is not that it is documentation. It is that it is the only path the procedure *forces*
to move between a check and the commit carrying that check's work, because the workflow requires the Outcome, the
status and the ticks before review is left. The journal, the drafts, the graph, the coverage baseline and the
reports are already outside the fingerprint. The copies `sync` generates are deliberately **not** tolerated, since
`sync` runs as part of the work and lands in the same commit as its source. No path may be added or removed
either: adding or deleting a file is not the procedure rewriting one.

Two places needed the same decision, and the second was not optional: the commit the search finds is usually the
docs commit whose whole diff is the ticket file, so counting that as what the round moved would have put the
ticket file into the comparison, where it has always moved since, and the fix would have bought nothing. A commit
that moved only the tolerated path did not carry the work, so the walk continues to its parent. An exact
fingerprint match is preferred throughout, the whole window being walked for one before any blob is tried,
because an exact match is the tree and a reader can verify it while a substituted match is a reconstruction.

The bound is unchanged at fifty commits, and the candidate blobs are only those the tolerated path held inside
that same window, taken from listings the exact pass already read, so the tolerance makes no additional git call.
Measured: 0.317s untolerated against 0.331s tolerated, and the worst case the bound allows, a distinct blob at
every commit with nothing matching, is under 0.4s.

**Nothing widened, measured rather than asserted.** 274 citations across every journal under
`docs/harness/history/`, each evaluated twice in one process with the tolerance on and forced off: no verdict
moved, and none of the 274 is cross-attempt. On SEEN-112, slices 1 and 2 are still refused by name on the files
attempts 3 and 4 reworked, the null round's green 24 is still refused, and green 33 is still held by no commit.
One verdict moved, slice 3's green 47 from refused to citable, and the reason is the one record 50 predicted:
the only difference between the tree that green ran against and the tree now is the ticket file the procedure
rewrote after it. No rework is hidden by the search, because there is no rework.

**And the bottom of it, which is a property rather than a defect.** A RED's tree can never be found, by this
mechanism or any other. A red runs on a tree holding the test without the code that answers it, and what gets
committed is the green. Measured: none of SEEN-112's five reds nor red 34 here is any commit's content, and a
brute-force sweep confirmed red 34's tree is not any of the last sixty commits' content modulo **any** single path.
So cross-attempt citation now works for a green and can never work for a red, and because the tdd gate requires
both halves of a slice entry, every cross-attempt slice pair still falls closed on its red.

Two rounds have now arrived at the same reading independently: **judge a slice's pair by its green.** A red's
standing does not rest on its tree at all. It rests on the ordering rule, which reads sequence numbers, and on its
own recorded failure, which the gate already checks from the record by requiring a non-zero exit and comparing the
stated reason. The red and the green in one slice entry are one round, so the round the green's commit carries is
the red's round too. That is a decision about what evidence means rather than a correction to code, it is the last
thing standing between this ticket and its own gate, and it is not one to take without being asked.
